title: Psalm 144: What Is Man, That You Regard Him?
summary: David blesses the LORD, his Rock, who trains his hands for battle and is his fortress, shield, and deliverer. Marveling that God takes notice of fleeting humans, he asks God to come down in storm and lightning and rescue him from deceitful foreigners, and promises a new song. The psalm closes with a picture of a nation at peace, with flourishing children, full barns, abundant flocks, and no breach in the walls, and declares blessed the people whose God is the LORD.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Royal psalms are about the king of Israel: his crowning, his wedding, his battles, God's promise to his family (Psalms 2, 18, 20, 21, 45, 72, 89, 101, 110, 132, 144).

line: David blesses the LORD his Rock, marvels that God regards fleeting human beings, asks for rescue, and pictures a people at peace whose God is the LORD.
guide: When you feel as small as a breath, remember that God stoops to think of you. Then ask what your picture of a good life is; the psalm ends with full barns and quiet streets, and says the real blessing is having the LORD as your God.

stanzas.title: Blessed be the LORD, my Rock and fortress
What is man, that you regard him?
Come down and rescue me from foreigners
A new song and a renewed plea
The blessing of a people whose God is the LORD

verses.t: Of David. Blessed be the LORD, my Rock, who trains my hands for war, my fingers for battle.
He is my steadfast love and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer. He is my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues peoples under me.
O LORD, what is man, that You regard him, the son of man that You think of him?
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
Part Your heavens, O LORD, and come down; touch the mountains, that they may smoke.
Flash forth Your lightning and scatter them; shoot Your arrows and rout them.
Reach down from on high; set me free and rescue me from the deep waters, from the grasp of foreigners,
whose mouths speak falsehood, whose right hands are deceitful.
I will sing to You a new song, O God; on a harp of ten strings I will make music to You—
to Him who gives victory to kings, who frees His servant David from the deadly sword.
Set me free and rescue me from the grasp of foreigners, whose mouths speak falsehood, whose right hands are deceitful.
Then our sons will be like plants nurtured in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved to adorn a palace.
Our storehouses will be full, supplying all manner of produce; our flocks will bring forth thousands, tens of thousands in our fields.
Our oxen will bear great loads. There will be no breach in the walls, no going into captivity, and no cry of lament in our streets.
Blessed are the people of whom this is so; blessed are the people whose God is the LORD.
